title: ChatGPT, Codex, Public Agent, and Private Agent Compatibility Expansion
objective: Allow the autonomous coordinator to discover, qualify, invoke, supervise, and verify Codex agents, ChatGPT agents, public plugins and apps, and personalized private agents without coupling core scheduling to a specific provider.
compatibility_assumption: Codex agents may expose skills, plugins, MCP servers, apps, commands, browser or computer-use tools, and worker callbacks.
ChatGPT agents may expose apps, connectors, actions, remote MCP servers, or conversational handoff surfaces with different execution and supervision semantics.
Public agents are untrusted external capabilities until their authority, privacy, authentication, and side-effect metadata are known.

Private personalized agents may be preferred project resources but remain independently versioned and immutable; project memory stores selection rules and outputs, not mutations to the agent or plugin.
A capability may be unavailable, unauthorized, incompatible, nonexistent, degraded, or ready; these states must not be collapsed into one failure mode.
global_invariants: The coordinator remains provider-neutral and never assumes that ChatGPT and Codex expose identical tools or lifecycle controls.
Agent identity, version, provenance, authority, data policy, credential reference, side-effect class, and invocation receipt are recorded for every delegated action.
Credentials remain project-local or host-managed and never enter plugin source, prompts, reports, dashboards, or canonical memory.
Computer use and other supervised actions cannot be delegated around the supervision boundary by using another agent.
PHI mode denies remote or public-agent disclosure and permits only explicitly qualified local synthetic-data workflows unless a stricter approved policy exists.
A failed or unavailable agent blocks only dependent slices; the coordinator continues alternative and independent work.
Agent outputs are proposals or evidence until admitted through schema, provenance, privacy, path-ownership, validation, and integration gates.

example_private_agent.name: SEO Decision Lab
preferred_flow: Discover the installed plugin and its exact version.
Run metadata-only authentication status before planning a live SEO invocation.
Select a shortcut tool when it satisfies the task; otherwise use the documented generic request surface.
Store the capability choice, market assumptions, request hash, cost or usage metadata, and redacted result provenance in project memory.
Treat missing expected credentials as a slice blocker, while continuing SEO-independent project work.
Validate returned SEO claims and generated implementation changes before integration.
